pending_commit.commit_message: UPSTREAM: gm45/gma.c: use screen on vga connector if connected The intel x4x and gm45 have very similar integrated graphic devices. Currently the x4x native graphic init enables VGA, while gm45 can output on LVDS. This patch reuses the x4x graphic initialisation code to enable output on VGA in gm45 in a way that the behavior is similar to vbios: If no VGA display is connected the internal LVDS screen is used. If an external screen is detected on the VGA port it will be used instead. BUG=None BRANCH=None TEST=None Signed-off-by: Arthur Heymans <arthur@aheymans.xyz> Reviewed-on: https://review.coreboot.org/16295 Tested-by: build bot (Jenkins) Reviewed-by: Martin Roth <martinroth@google.com> Reviewed-by: Paul Menzel <paulepanter@users.sourceforge.net> Change-Id: I7e9ff793a5384ad8b4220fb1c0d9b28e6cee8391 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/388108 Commit-Ready: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: Makefile.inc: Add aliases for submodule updates to gitconfig target Updating submodules seem to give people headaches, so this adds a pair of git aliases to update them. 'git sup' updates the submodules to the latest versions, but leaves any locally modified files. 'git sup-destroy' will remove the current submodules and re-initialize them. This deletes any local changes. process_utils: add ppid to IsProcessAlive When we checked if a process is alive or not, only pid was given. However, if the process is actually terminated, and unfortunately a new process is running with the same PID, then we are checking on an irrelevant process. By providing ppid (parent PID) of given process, we can be more confident that we are watching the correct process. The ppid argument is optional, without this argument, the function checks process status only. Remove board factory wiping/cutoff scripts. Chromebooks used to perform wiping and battery cut-off in release image, which adds dependency to several factory-only (or RMA) scripts, image files and tools (usually 'ectool' from ec-utils package). This is not a preferred approach because (1) These scripts may change due to factory requests, which caused a process of requesting FSI change. (2) The scripts may have information related to factory environment (for example shopfloor IP) that should not stay in release image. (3) Cut-off tools, especially if it is using some proprietary programs or accessing particular ports, may have security exploit. As a result, factory software has been changed to 'in-place-wiping' and included battery cut-off ( http://crbug.com/544021 ). Now it is time to remove all legacy wiping scripts.
